title: Characteristics of the short rachillae of rice from archaeological sites dating to 7000 years ago
version: Chinese Science Bulletin 52, 1654–1660 (2007), DOI 10.1007/s11434-007-0258-1; publisher PDF.
lineage: Original morphological analysis of rice grains and husks from excavated material, distinct from the sediment microfossils examined by Zong and colleagues.

passages.note: The authors assign 70 of the 120 short rachillae they examined from Kuahuqiao to wild type and 50 to a japonica type, and infer early rice cultivation. Morphological categories and samples do not identify individual fields or exact generations of plants.

The team separately reports examples of wild-type and japonica-type rachilla markings in Shangshan and Xiaohuangshan material. Their rice material and morphology differ from the dated Shangshan silica samples analysed by Zuo and colleagues.
